one_month_reasoning: Full Q3-26 results are expected around Nov 9-10, after Oct 31. But TeraWulf put out PRELIMINARY Q3-25 results on Oct 28 2025 alongside a deal announcement (source 31), so a late-October preliminary print or deal release is possible and could cut either way. Other events in the window: confirmation of CB-4 first-hall delivery and rent start (in commissioning, no release yet; mild +); a possible launch or pricing of the ~$3.5B Justified debt (Hut 8's IG project notes, sources 25-26, show the market is open for IG-backed leases, but there was still no WULF release as of Oct 1, source 30; +/-); the Oct 28 FOMC; and AI-capex sentiment across CIFR/HUT/IREN. Momentum is negative (-50% from the June high) and the consensus target ($33, source 29) is far above spot, so these roughly offset. I centre just below spot ($14.80) with lognormal monthly sigma ~26% (91%/3.5), symmetric. I did not lean on my below-spot fair value, because valuation barely moves a stock within one month. Round 4: the site and discount-rate fixes are valuation changes and do not move a 1-month forecast. Two more in-window items, each small and of uncertain sign: a possible Chesapeake closing (price disclosure) and the Lansing draft ban (Lake Hawkeye is only ~$0.22/sh in my model). The 1-month ladder is unchanged.

fair_value.method: Valued at Oct-2027: 50% split-rate DCF covering every site ($4.66 contracted + $2.65 pipeline = $7.31/sh; IG-backed contracted rents at 8.0%, unrated at 9.25%, Anthropic 9.5%, everything else at the 10.5% WACC; single-rate DCF $6.40) and 50% 13x 2028 EBITDA of $1.03B less $8.79B net debt, remaining Justified capex, minority put and Chesapeake price, over 615M shares ($7.47) => ~$7.4.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Split-rate, site-by-site unlevered DCF at Oct-27. Contracted in-term rents: Fluidstack $7.2B/10 yrs at 3% escalator (44% Google-backstopped at 8.0%, 56% at 9.25%), Core42 $110M/yr to 2035 at 9.25%, Anthropic $19B/20 yrs at 2% at 9.5% (incl. $1.6B post-Oct-27 capex and the $150M minority put). Post-term (tenant 5-yr options at contract escalators, 60%/75% exercise; else vacancy, $1.5M/MW retrofit, re-let 80% at 85%), mining, pipeline and TV at the 10.5% WACC. EV $9.77B - net debt $6.90B = $4.66/sh contracted; pipeline (LM-EXP, Lake Hawkeye, Muskie, Chesapeake) $1.63B = $2.65/sh; total $7.31. Single rate 10.5%: $3.75 + $2.65 = $6.40. GPU life 5/6/7 yrs: split $6.03/$7.31/$8.22, single $5.13/$6.40/$7.31. Sensitivities (split): Anthropic at 8.0% if IG support is finalized +$0.98; WACC 10%/11% $8.57/$6.20; IG rate ±50bp ∓$0.04; unrated rate ±50bp ∓$0.06.

inputs_detail.value: Cash flows from Q4-27 to 2060 valued at Oct 1 2027, mid-period discounting (rents are paid monthly); TV after 2060 at WACC, g=1%
inputs_detail.derivation: Round 3 was rebuilt from scratch in round 4. An end-of-year convention would lower the single-rate contracted DCF by ~$0.76/sh; mid-period is the standard for monthly rent.

inputs_detail.input: Lake Mariner Fluidstack leases (CB-3 42 MW, CB-4 168 MW, CB-5 168 MW = 378 MW)
inputs_detail.value: $7.2B over the 10-yr initial terms ($6.7B + ~$0.5B July-2026 amendments), 3%/yr escalator => year-1 rent ~$628M for 378 MW (~$1.66M/MW), ~$646M in 2028, ~$819M by year 10; commencement CB-3 Jul-26, CB-4 ~Dec-26 (unconfirmed), CB-5 ~Mar-27
inputs_detail.derivation: Contract totals from the inventory. The escalator is not disclosed: 3% is implied by $3.7B initial vs ~$8.7B including two 5-yr extensions (1.03^10 = 1.34 = $5.0B/$3.7B). Round 3 used a flat $720M/yr. MW changed from ~360 to 378 (10-Q/deck). The end user's silicon (Google TPUs) is not company-disclosed and is no longer used as evidence.

inputs_detail.value: 44% of in-term Fluidstack rent at the contracted (IG-backed) rate 8.0%, 56% at the unrated rate 9.25%
inputs_detail.derivation: Google (Aa2/AA+) backstops ~$3.2B of the $7.2B ($1.8B CB-3/CB-4 + $1.4B CB-5), effective per lease at commencement; all three will have commenced by the Oct-27 valuation date. Google's right: pay a termination fee or assume the lease (Google pays WULF). Pro-rata split because the backstop is sized to the notes, not to the full rent.

inputs_detail.value: ~$110M/yr flat to ~end-2035 (10 yrs from Jul-25 to Mar-26 phased commencement); ~$4M residual prepaid-rent offset in Q4-27; discounted at 9.25%
inputs_detail.derivation: Inventory: TCV ~$1.1B over 10 yrs (Q3-25 release; single-source), which I prefer to my round-3 $100M (built from the $90M prepaid first-year base rent) because it is the company's own contract total. MW 60 (10-Q) replaces 72.5 (2025 releases). $50.6M deferred rent at 6/30/26, applied to 50% of base rent, is almost used up by Oct-27. Core42 is unrated with no backstop.

inputs_detail.value: $19B over 20 yrs, ASSUMED 2% escalator => ~$782M full-year start; phased 30% from ~Nov-27 ($59M in Q4-27), 70% from ~Apr-28 (2028 ~$646M); discounted at 9.5%
inputs_detail.derivation: Escalator not disclosed (2% is mine; flat or 3% changes the DCF by about +$0.55/-$0.25). Rate 9.5%: Anthropic is not rated (S&P), the IG credit support is 'expected', not final, and the campus is pre-completion at the valuation date. The planned ~$3.5B financing is leveraged loans plus high yield (Bloomberg), i.e. sub-IG, so the unrated rate plus 25bp for completion risk. If IG support is finalized, 8.0% gives +$0.98/sh.

inputs_detail.value: Tenant options modelled explicitly. 6-yr base: P(exercise first 5-yr option) 60% (Core42 50%), P(second | first) 75% (Core42 70%), both at the contract escalator. Non-exercise: 12-month vacancy, $1.5M/MW landlord retrofit, P(re-let) 80% at 85% of expiring rent then +2%/yr. Expected post-term factor ~0.89. All post-term flows at the 10.5% WACC
inputs_detail.derivation: Replaces round 3's uniform 95%-of-expiring-rent +1%/yr re-lease. The options are the tenant's right, so they are exercised only when renewal is cheaper than the market, which caps the upside. The ~0.89 factor sits inside the supervisor's 0.85-0.91 band and the 20-35% CREFC renewal stress. Same structure for Anthropic's two 5-yr options after ~2048.

inputs_detail.input: Lease NOI margin, G&A, maintenance, tax
inputs_detail.value: 82% NOI; $120M/yr G&A allocated pro-rata to revenue; 3% maintenance capex from 2029; cash tax 12% of EBITDA from 2030
inputs_detail.derivation: Unchanged from round 3. G&A and other costs are allocated to each contract and discounted at that contract's rate.

inputs_detail.value: $11M/MW x 401 MW = $4.41B incl. site, less $353M already contributed at 6/30/26 = $4.06B remaining: $0.40B 2H26, $2.75B 2027, $0.91B 2028; $2.46B before Oct-27 (net debt), $1.60B after (in DCF at 9.5%)
inputs_detail.derivation: Fix: round 3 spread the whole $4.41B from 2H26 although $353M (incl. the $200M site) was already in the June-30 balance sheet (10-Q, inventory).

inputs_detail.value: -$150M paid ~2029 (fixed-amount put from 1st anniversary of operations; the seller has the right and WULF pays)
inputs_detail.derivation: Flag fix. The 10-Q gives a fixed amount but not the figure; fair value at acquisition was $100.6M (Feb-26). Accreted ~3 yrs at ~13% => ~$150M. Discounted at the Anthropic rate.

inputs_detail.value: $6.90B: Jun-26 face debt $5,725M less $3,028M cash (incl. $410M restricted) = $2,697M; + $295M Muskie utility cash collateral (posted Jul-26, not free); - $530M Abernathy proceeds; + $1,700M LM capex + $150M parent-funded tenant fit-out; + $2,463M Justified capex to Q3-27; + $50M Muskie deferred consideration (May-27); + $450M interest; - $370M operating cash flow. Converts at face
inputs_detail.derivation: Round 3 had $6.65B. Added Muskie collateral (+$295M), fit-out (+$150M; deck: 'WULF contributing ~$150M to fund tenant fit-out costs incurred through June 30 2026', excluded from the $1.7B; if it was already paid by Jun-30 this is +$0.24/sh) and Muskie deferred (+$50M). Justified capex corrected (-$240M).
Company treasury-method table (612.9M at $16), which includes the 73.6M Google penny warrants (WULF granted these to Google, so they dilute WULF holders) and net shares on in-the-money converts.

inputs_detail.value: ~$5M/yr gross profit to end-2028, then the power goes to the LM expansion; +$0.01/sh
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2-26 digital-asset revenue $12.8M against mostly power costs (10-Q), so near break-even even with hashprice up ~40% since July. Stopped in 2029 so its power is not also counted in LM-EXP.

inputs_detail.input: Pipeline sites (each probability-weighted, net of capex, 2% financing fees, contingent consideration and collateral, at the 10.5% WACC)
inputs_detail.value: LM-EXP 162 MW p35% $0.37; Lake Hawkeye 320 MW p15% $0.22; Muskie 400+400 MW p55%/35% $1.80; Chesapeake 400+400 MW p(close) 90% x p35%/20% $0.26 net of ~$150M price; total $1.63B = $2.65/sh
inputs_detail.derivation: New lease: $2.1M/MW-yr start, +2.5%/yr, 15 yrs (Anthropic $2.37M avg, Fluidstack $1.86M, Hut 8 15-yr terms), NOI 82% less maintenance and tax, $11M/MW capex ($10M at the brownfield LM; +$1.5M/MW at Chesapeake for on-site generation), 60% residual after the term => ~$3.1M/MW NPV at a 2029 COD. Muskie also deducts $90k/MW-gross contingent consideration and models $565M of utility collateral, returned on success and half lost on failure. The Chesapeake price is undisclosed (confidential at FERC, TheBayNet), so $150M is my estimate.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 13x 2028 EBITDA $1.03B = $13.39B EV; less $6.90B Oct-27 net debt, $1.60B post-Oct-27 Justified capex, $0.15B Justified minority put and $0.135B probability-weighted Chesapeake price = $4.59B / 615M = $7.47. Cross-check: 13x 2029 EBITDA ($1.17B) discounted one year = $8.05.

inputs_detail.derivation: Contracted revenue $1.40B in 2028 (Fluidstack $646M on the escalated schedule, Core42 $110M, Anthropic $646M phased) x 82% - $120M G&A. Down from round 3's $1.10B because Fluidstack rent is now escalated from a lower start instead of flat at its $720M average (same contract total) and Anthropic is phased.
Unchanged: low end of UBS's 13-18x 2028 comp range.

Net debt as in the DCF, now including Muskie collateral and deferred consideration and the LM fit-out; plus the Justified minority put and Chesapeake price (flag fixes). The multiple is taken to cover pipeline optionality, so no separate pipeline credit.

bear.story: The Justified $3.5B leveraged-loan/HY package prices wide or slips, or Anthropic's IG support is not finalized; CB-4/CB-5 or Justified delays; the Lansing ban and NY EO 62 shut the NY pipeline; AI-infra de-rating. The market values WULF between my contracted-only DCF ($3.75 single-rate, $4.66 split) and contracted plus pipeline, with convert overhang and possible dilution.

base.story: Lake Mariner fully delivered (438 MW leased), Justified financed and on track for late-2027 first capacity, maybe one Muskie lease. The stock trades between fundamental value (~$7.4; ~$8.3 if Anthropic's IG support lowers its rate) and peer-multiple value plus a pipeline premium, with sector beta dominating.

bull.story: Anthropic IPO and IG rating, a 400 MW Muskie lease toward the 250-500 MW/yr target, Justified debt at IG-like spreads as Hut 8 achieved, and a re-rating toward 15-18x forward EBITDA (UBS $24 / consensus $33 territory).

thesis_break_reason: Round 4, with every site counted once: contracted-only DCF $3.75 at a single 10.5% rate, $4.66 with contract-appropriate rates; contracted plus probability-weighted pipeline $6.40 / $7.31. A sustained close below ~$6 means the market gives the four pipeline campuses (2,082 MW) little or no value and doubts the contracted cash flows or their financing: a failed or punitive Justified raise, Anthropic's IG support not finalized, Fluidstack credit trouble before the Google backstop matters, a major CB-5/Justified delay, or a dilutive rescue raise. That is a fundamental break, not 91%-vol noise. Kept at $6.0: the split-rate contracted DCF (+$0.9) is offset by the new site deductions (Muskie collateral, fit-out, minority put, Chesapeake price).

Discount rate: the split-rate DCF adds only ~$0.9/sh over single-rate because the IG-backed slice (44% of Fluidstack in-term rent) is short-duration; WACC 10% vs 11% moves the split DCF $8.6 vs $6.2

Post-term option exercise (tenant's right) after 2035-48; GPU life 5 vs 7 yrs moves the split DCF $6.0-8.2/sh
CB-4 commencement still unconfirmed by release as of Oct 2; revolver capped at $75M until it happens
reasoning: Round 2 fixes the errors the supervisor verified in my bridge. Shares go from 714M if-converted to ~615M from the company's treasury-method cap table, with converts as debt at $2.525B face. I had swapped the 2031/2032 principals: the 2031 is $1,000M at $12.43 and the 2032 is $1,025M at $19.94. Justified capex goes from $9.5M to $11M/MW ($4.41B). The multiples method now deducts post-Oct-27 Justified capex, and WACC goes from 10% to a consistent 10.5%. Net effect: contracted-only DCF ~$3.0 and pipeline credit $2.4 (cut for higher capex and WACC), so the DCF is $5.4. The DCF stays as one of my methods, as requested, with these corrections. I replaced the EV/sales leg, which rested on one press source (Rallies) the supervisor discounted, with EV/EBITDA, using UBS's Sep-23 comp range (13-18x 2028 EBITDA; CORZ ~12x) at the low end (13x) for leverage and concentration: $9.6. The blend is $7.7, versus $11.1 in round 1 and the supervisor's ~$9.3 estimate for my corrected model. Mine is lower mainly because of 10.5% vs 10% WACC, a smaller pipeline credit and the switch from EV/sales to EV/EBITDA. New industry evidence cuts both ways. Hut 8 financed IG-backed AI leases with IG project notes (River Bend $3.25B, Beacon Point $4.25B Baa2, ~90-95% LTC), so the Justified debt is financeable if Anthropic's credit support is finalized, and the cost of capital for contracted MW is lower than parent WACC implies. That is the main reason I do not drag the median all the way to fair value. The sell side is far more bullish (25 brokers, avg $33; UBS $24 citing ~$12M equity value per MW), and the market clearly pays for the pipeline. I set the 12-month median at ~$12.8 (pulled ~30% of the way from spot toward my $7.7 fair value, the same proportional pull as round 1) with lognormal sigma ~0.82 (slightly fatter tails for the binary financing and lease events), giving bear/base/bull of $5.5/$12.5/$26 at 25/50/25. Limits: ~8 follow-up queries; Twelve Data/Alpha Vantage not used; no option data or priors consulted. ROUND 3 (GPU useful life): WULF is a powered-shell landlord, so the GPU-life research applies only partially. The rents inside the initial terms (Fluidstack to 2036, Core42 to 2035, Anthropic to 2048) are valued at contract price and do not depend on GPU economics; Fluidstack owns no chips and Google backstops $3.2B. What changed: post-term re-leasing is now tied to a 6-year base tenant GPU life (renewal 80% Lake Mariner / 75% Core42, re-lease at 95% of expiring rent, $1.5M/MW retrofit), the TV renewal haircut now applies only to the Justified share (fixing a double haircut), and a ~$175M Q4-27 Lake Mariner capex double count was removed per the supervisor's revisit. Net: contracted DCF $3.0 -> $3.2, DCF $5.4 -> $5.6 (5 yrs $4.6, 7 yrs $6.2), fair value $7.7 -> $7.8. A $0.1 move in fair value shifts the ladder median by ~$0.03 under my 30% pull, so the 12-month ladder, 1-month ladder, scenarios and $6.0 thesis break are unchanged. One search used (Fluidstack/Lake Mariner TPU structure and extension options). ROUND 4 (site coverage and split-rate discounting): I rebuilt the DCF site by site from the inventory. MW are now 60 Core42 + 378 Fluidstack. Core42 is $1.1B/10 yrs (company total). Fluidstack rent is $7.2B at a 3% escalator implied by the extension-value disclosure. I fixed the flags: Justified 6.8% minority put (-$150M), Muskie collateral (+$295M in net debt) and deferred/contingent consideration, the $150M parent fit-out, Chesapeake's undisclosed price (est. $150M, 90% close), mining added through 2028 with its power then reassigned to the LM expansion, and the NY pipeline cut for the Lansing ban and EO 62. Lake Hawkeye, LM-EXP, Muskie and Chesapeake are each valued separately. The Justified capex double count of the $353M already spent was also fixed. Per the supervisor, post-term renewal is now tenant option exercise at the contract escalator versus vacancy, retrofit and re-let (~0.89 expected factor), not a uniform 95%/+1% re-lease. Discounting: Google-backstopped Fluidstack rent at 8.0% (anchored on the 7.75%/8.7%-effective BB WULF Compute notes secured on these leases, below them for the Aa2 backstop slice and post-completion, above Hut 8's IG project paper); unrated Fluidstack and Core42 at 9.25%; Anthropic at 9.5% (unrated, pre-completion, HY financing); everything else at 10.5%. Result: single-rate DCF $6.40 ($3.75 contracted + $2.65 pipeline) and split-rate $7.31 ($4.66 + $2.65), against round 3's $5.6 single-rate ($3.2 + $2.4). Of the single-rate rise, ~$0.76 is the mid-period convention of the rebuild and ~$0.6 is the escalated rent shape feeding higher extension rents; the site deductions (-$0.9) offset most of the remaining gains. EV/EBITDA falls to $7.47 because 2028 EBITDA is $1.03B on the escalated schedule (the contract total is unchanged) and the deductions are larger. Blend 50/50 (the DCF now covers every site): $7.4, from $7.8. Under my 30% pull, the 12-month median moves from ~$12.8 to ~$12.7, so the ladder shifts down by ~0.002-0.005. Scenarios move base $12.5 -> $12.4; the thesis break stays $6.0 and the 1-month ladder is unchanged. Research: 3 searches (Morgantown price, Justified financing, Lansing ban) plus direct reads of the 10-Q and Q2 deck.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Not applied to WULF's own revenue: it leases powered shells at contract rent. In-term rent is held at the contract schedule. GPU life enters after the initial terms through the tenant's option exercise and re-letting. 6 yrs: P(first 5-yr option) 60% / P(second) 75% at the contract escalator; otherwise 12-month vacancy, $1.5M/MW retrofit, 80% re-let at 85% of expiring rent then +2%/yr. 5 yrs: 45%/65%, 18-month vacancy, $2.0M/MW, 75% re-let at 75%, plus 5% expected loss on unbacked Fluidstack rent 2030-36. 7 yrs: 70%/80%, 9-month vacancy, $1.0M/MW, 85% re-let at 95%. Core42 option odds are 10pp (first) and 5pp (second) lower.
gpu_life.note: Split-rate DCF incl. pipeline (single-rate: $5.13/$6.40/$7.31). Contracted-only split: $3.38/$4.66/$5.58. Base kept at 6 yrs: the fact-checked company lives are CoreWeave 6, Nebius 5, IREN 5, and supervisor feedback says 6 is acceptable for a shell lessor. Post-term flows are discounted at WACC. The EV/EBITDA leg is unaffected.

discounting.basis: Anchor: WULF Compute $3.2B 7.750% senior secured notes (8.7% effective incl. $105M fees; Ba2/BB/BB at issue) are secured on the Fluidstack and Core42 leases, with the Google backstop sized to the notes. I apply 8.0% to the Google-backstopped (Aa2/AA+) share of in-term Fluidstack rent (44% = $3.2B/$7.2B). That is below the notes' 8.7%, because that pool also carries unbacked Fluidstack and unrated Core42 rent and construction risk that ends by Oct-27. It is above Hut 8's IG project notes (SOFR+240 / Baa2) to leave a completion and operating premium. Unrated in-term rent (56% of Fluidstack; Core42 with only $90M prepaid) is at 9.25%: above the pool's effective cost, below WACC. Anthropic is at 9.5%: unrated per S&P, IG support 'expected', not final, pre-completion, and the planned financing is leveraged loans plus HY. At 8.0% if IG support is finalized: +$0.98/sh. Post-term, pipeline, mining and terminal flows are at the 10.5% WACC. The split adds only +$0.91/sh because the IG-backed slice is short-dated.
